journal_name: Journal of Network and Computer Applications

abstracts.abstract: The proliferation of edge computing paradigms has fundamentally transformed distributed computing architectures, yet existing task offloading frameworks fail to capture the dynamic complexity of multi-edge environments. This paper introduces a novel stochastic computing paradigm based on Markov Decision Processes with Recursive Reward Modeling (MDP-RRM) for intelligent task offloading in edge networks. Unlike conventional approaches that treat edge resources as static entities, our framework conceptualizes edge nodes as adaptive computing agents that continuously learn and optimize offloading decisions through recursive reward feedback loops. We formalize the offloading problem as a partially observable Markov decision process and derive optimal policies using deep reinforcement learning with reward decomposition. Theoretical analysis proves the convergence of our algorithm to Pareto-optimal offloading strategies with computational complexity O(n log n), where n represents the number of edge nodes. Extensive simulations across diverse network topologies demonstrate that the MDP-RRM paradigm achieves 47% improvement in task completion latency and 38% reduction in energy consumption compared to state-of-the-art methods. This paradigm shift from static resource allocation to adaptive agent-based computing provides a foundational framework for next-generation edge intelligence, fundamentally advancing the theoretical understanding of distributed computing in heterogeneous edge environments.

Network function virtualization (NFV) has emerged as a critical technology for flexible service function chaining, but existing queuing models inadequately capture the stochastic behavior of virtualized network functions under dynamic workloads. This paper presents an enhanced analytical framework incorporating fractional Brownian motion (fBm) to characterize long-range dependence in NFV traffic. We extend the classical Jackson network model by introducing Hurst parameter-dependent service rates and deriving closed-form expressions for mean queue length and waiting time distributions. The proposed fBm-NFV model addresses the significant limitation of traditional exponential assumptions that fail to represent heavy-tailed traffic patterns prevalent in modern cloud applications. Our analysis reveals that the correlation structure of traffic significantly impacts NFV service chain performance, with the Hurst parameter showing strong influence on end-to-end latency (R² = 0.94). Compared to existing models, our framework reduces prediction error by 34% for high-variance traffic scenarios and provides accurate performance bounds for service function chains with up to 10 virtualized functions. The improved analytical tractability enables more efficient NFV resource provisioning and admission control policies, substantially advancing network management capabilities in virtualized infrastructures.

The convergence of Internet of Things (IoT) and edge computing presents unprecedented challenges for real-time data processing, yet current architectures suffer from rigid data pipelines and inefficient resource utilization. This paper introduces EdgeFlow, a novel edge-native data streaming architecture that fundamentally reimagines IoT data processing through intent-based flow orchestration. EdgeFlow introduces three revolutionary components: (1) a hierarchical intent abstraction layer that translates high-level application requirements into distributed flow policies, (2) adaptive computation placement engines that dynamically relocate processing functions based on real-time network conditions, and (3) collaborative edge clusters enabling cross-edge data sharing without centralized coordination. The system implements a completely decentralized control plane using distributed consensus algorithms, eliminating single points of failure inherent in traditional cloud-edge architectures. We deployed EdgeFlow across 200 heterogeneous edge nodes spanning smart city deployments and conducted extensive evaluation over 180 days of real-world operation. Results demonstrate 56% reduction in data processing latency, 72% improvement in network resource utilization, and graceful degradation under network partitions. EdgeFlow represents a paradigm shift from cloud-centric to edge-native design principles, establishing a new architectural foundation for latency-sensitive IoT applications including autonomous systems and industrial automation.

Software-defined networking (SDN) has revolutionized network management, but existing security mechanisms inadequately address the increasing sophistication of distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks targeting control plane integrity. This paper presents SecuSDN, an enhanced security architecture that substantially improves DDoS detection and mitigation in SDN environments through multi-layer collaborative defense. SecuSDN introduces three significant improvements: (1) a lightweight flow-based anomaly detection module operating at line rate using compressed sensing techniques, achieving detection latency under 50 milliseconds, (2) an intelligent rate-limiting mechanism combining machine learning predictions with programmable data plane actions for automatic threat response, and (3) a cross-controller synchronization protocol enabling coordinated defense across multiple SDN domains. The architecture preserves backward compatibility with OpenFlow specifications while introducing novel security extensions. We implemented SecuSDN on commodity hardware and evaluated its effectiveness against realistic attack scenarios including volumetric floods, protocol exploits, and application-layer attacks. Experimental results demonstrate 89% detection accuracy with false positive rates below 2%, achieving attack mitigation response times of 120 milliseconds—representing a 65% improvement over existing solutions. SecuSDN provides substantial advancement in network security for SDN deployments while maintaining the programmability and flexibility that characterize software-defined architectures.
